A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
fixpoint logics over ordered structures are the natural logics for complexity classes.

the complexity of fixpoint queries over ordered structures is completely determined by the choice of fixpoint operators and iteration constructs, and the complexity of fixpoints over arbitrary structures is determined by the choice and the interaction between fixpoint operators and structures.

the choice of iteration construct (deterministic vs. nondeterministic vs. alternating) has a significant impact on the computational complexity of the fixpoint logic.
